samf-junior-1998-r1-02.title: Half of 50
samf-junior-1998-r1-02.body:
$50\%$ is one half, and half of 50 is 25.

**Answer: (C) 25**

samf-junior-1998-r1-03.title: Estimate and check the last digit
samf-junior-1998-r1-03.body:
$12.34-1.234\approx 11.1$, so the answer is near 11.1. The last digit: thousandths $0-4$ borrows to give $6$, so only $11.106$ fits.

**Answer: (A) 11.106**

samf-junior-1998-r1-06.title: Count rows and columns
samf-junior-1998-r1-06.body:
Rows: $3+4-1=6$ (John's row is counted from both ends). Desks per row: $3+5-1=7$. Total $6\times7=42$ desks.

**Answer: (D) 42**

samf-junior-1998-r1-07.title: Try the middle guess
samf-junior-1998-r1-07.body:
The guesses are 23, 25, 27, 29, 31. If the number is 27, then 25 and 29 are off by 2, 23 and 31 are off by 4, and 27 is correct. This matches exactly.

**Answer: (B) 27**

samf-junior-1998-r1-07.title: Rule out the others
samf-junior-1998-r1-07.body:
If the correct guess were 25, then 23 and 27 would be off by 2, but 29 and 31 are off by 4 and 6. The only guess with two guesses on each side at distances 2 and 4 is the middle one. 27 is the answer.

**Answer: (B) 27**

samf-junior-1998-r1-09.title: List the side pairs
samf-junior-1998-r1-09.body:
The perimeter is 16, so length plus width is 8. The pairs (length $\ge$ width) are $7\times1$, $6\times2$, $5\times3$, $4\times4$. A square is a rectangle, so there are 4.

**Answer: (C) 4**

samf-junior-1998-r1-10.title: Count along the circumference
samf-junior-1998-r1-10.body:
The circumference is 100 cm, and each triangle has a side of 5 cm on the edge of the band, so $100\div5=20$ triangles point one way. The triangles pointing the other way fill the gaps between them, another 20. In total $20+20=40$.

**Answer: (B) 40**

samf-junior-1998-r1-11.title: Common denominator
samf-junior-1998-r1-11.body:
$\frac12=\frac6{12}$ and $\frac23=\frac8{12}$, so $\frac7{12}$ lies between them. Check the others: $\frac{17}{24}=0.708$, $\frac13$, $\frac14$ are too small or too large, and $\frac34=0.75$ exceeds $\frac23$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac7{12}$**

samf-junior-1998-r1-13.title: Weeks
samf-junior-1998-r1-13.body:
$45=6\times7+3$, so 45 days contain six full weeks (6 Mondays) plus 3 extra days. If the first of the 45 days is a Monday, the extra days are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and we get a 7th Monday. A 8th is impossible, since 8 Mondays need $7\times7+1=50$ days.

**Answer: (C) 7**

samf-junior-1998-r1-17.title: Try powers
samf-junior-1998-r1-17.body:
Powers of 2: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. Powers of 3: 3, 9, 27. We need a sum of 41: $32+9=41$. So $x=5$, $y=2$ and $x+y=7$. (Other pairs fail: $41-16=25$, $41-8=33$, $41-4=37$, $41-2=39$ are not powers of 3.)

**Answer: (C) 7**

samf-junior-1998-r1-18.title: Cycle of last digits
samf-junior-1998-r1-18.body:
Last digits of $3,9,27,81,243,\dots$ are $3,9,7,1,3,9,7,1,\dots$ repeating every 4. Since $100$ is a multiple of 4, $3^{100}$ ends in 1.

**Answer: (B) 1**

samf-junior-1998-r1-18.title: Use $3^4=81$
samf-junior-1998-r1-18.body:
$3^{100}=(3^4)^{25}=81^{25}$, and a number ending in 1 raised to any power ends in 1.

**Answer: (B) 1**

samf-junior-1998-r1-19.title: Equation
samf-junior-1998-r1-19.body:
Let $m$ be the number of misses. Then $4(20-m)-6m=30$, so $80-10m=30$ and $m=5$.

**Answer: (A) 5**

samf-junior-1998-r1-20.title: Work backwards
samf-junior-1998-r1-20.body:
After shop 4: R3 left, so before shop 4 he had R6. Before shop 3: he spent half plus R1, so if he had $y$ then $\frac y2-1=6$, giving $y=14$. Before shop 2: $\frac z2-1=14$, so $z=30$. Before shop 1: $\frac x2-2=30$, so $x=64$.

**Answer: (D) R64**

samf-junior-1998-r1-20.title: Equation
samf-junior-1998-r1-20.body:
If he starts with $x$, he has $\frac x2-2$, then $\frac x4-2$, then $\frac x8-2$ left, and after shop 4 half of that: $\frac12(\frac x8-2)=3$. So $\frac x8=8$, $x=64$.

**Answer: (D) R64**
